Consult Summary:
- 4-week postpartum patient with acute-onset shortness of breath for one hour and a cough since yesterday; clinician concerned about possible thromboembolic event related to recent C-section and advised urgent hospital evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: acute shortness of breath and cough.
- Timeline:
  - C-section performed approximately 4 weeks ago.
  - Cough began yesterday (nonproductive; no sputum reported).
  - Shortness of breath began about one hour prior to the consult while sitting and watching TV and is described as acute in onset.
  - Patient palpated her pulse during the consult and counted 30 beats during the instructed counting interval.
  - Patient reports intermittent codeine use for post-op pain, taken fairly regularly after C-section but not taken for approximately one week.
- Symptom characteristics and progression:
  - Shortness of breath: sudden onset, while at rest; patient feels palpitations ("my heart is really going").
  - Cough: started yesterday; no sputum produced.
  - Chest: no constant chest pain; chest feels sore on deep inspiration; C-section scar is tender.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating or relieving factors identified.
  - Patient advised not to take codeine prior to hospital evaluation.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems (as mentioned):
  - Palpitations/tachycardia sensation.
  - No documented fever, syncope, leg pain or swelling, hemoptysis, or other systemic complaints.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior episodes of similar shortness of breath reported.
  - Baby is well; no cough or cold in baby.

Past Medical History:
- Recent obstetric history: Cesarean section approximately 4 weeks ago (postoperative course not further detailed).
- No other chronic medical problems reported.
- Family history: mother has history of clots in her legs.

Medications:
- Codeine — taken postoperatively; dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports it was used fairly regularly but not in the last week.
- No other medications documented.

Allergies:
- Ibuprofen — reaction not documented (patient unable to describe what happens with ibuprofen).

Social History:
- Mother of newborn; baby present at home.
- Partner currently at work; patient is alone at home at time of consult.
- Smoking, alcohol, and substance use: not documented.
- No financial or other lifestyle issues documented.

Family History:
- Mother with history of leg clots (deep venous thrombosis) as stated by patient.

Physical Examination:
- No formal clinician-performed vitals or physical exam documented.
- Patient-performed pulse check: patient counted 30 beats during the instructed counting interval (context: clinician noted heart "running slightly fast" based on this count).
- Reported findings on self-exam: chest soreness on deep inspiration; tender C-section scar.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath with palpitations in the context of recent (4-week) C-section — concern for possible venous thromboembolism (pulmonary embolism).
  - Plan:
    - Urgent evaluation in hospital emergency department recommended.
    - Options discussed: ambulance transport (offered) versus self-transport; patient elected to go to hospital herself with baby.
    - Advised to go promptly and bring supplies for baby.
    - Advised to withhold codeine prior to hospital evaluation.
    - If thromboembolism is confirmed in hospital, anticoagulation can be started as appropriate (noted by clinician).
- Issue 2: Acute cough (onset yesterday), nonproductive.
  - Plan:
    - To be evaluated during hospital assessment (part of ED workup).
- Issue 3: Postoperative pain and tender C-section scar with recent analgesic use (codeine).
  - Plan:
    - Wound and pain to be assessed in hospital; review of analgesia and management to be done there.
- General plan items:
  - If symptoms worsen or patient becomes more unwell, seek immediate emergency services/consider calling an ambulance.
  - ED evaluation to include assessment for DVT/PE and appropriate imaging and labs as indicated (not specified in transcript; clinician advised that hospital can provide treatment if clot found).

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but expected clinical elements:
  - Vital signs (heart rate numeric value, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation) are not documented.
  - Formal clinician physical examination findings (cardiovascular, respiratory, extremities for DVT signs) not documented.
  - Details of obstetric course, any perioperative complications, or thromboprophylaxis status after C-section not documented.
  - Exact codeine dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Details of ibuprofen allergic reaction not documented.
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use history not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Conflict noted in date of birth: patient stated 20 April 1980; clinician repeated as 1983. (DOB discrepancy documented.)
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/transcription quality sufficient; content clear and audible with minimal background noise.
